clue.text: A brave tribe, but strangely unattractive

indicators.note: done strangely means done in an odd way, so the letters before it come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: all eleven letters of the phrase are the raw material

explanation.surface: A courageous tribe is described as, oddly, not very pleasant to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebarbative is a formal word for repellent or objectionable, so it is a close synonym of unattractive.

clue.text: Dr Rory, a Scotsman, doctored in a Scottish county once

indicators.note: something doctored has been tampered with, so these letters have been rearranged

blocks.note: every letter of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: A Scottish doctor called Rory has himself been medically treated somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross and Cromarty was a county in the far north of Scotland until 1975. 'Doctored' plays on the Dr in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ross and Cromarty existed as a Scottish administrative shire until local government reorganisation abolished the old counties in 1975.

clue.text: British have Scottish Chancellor

blocks.note: Br is the standard abbreviation for British
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Britain is said to possess a Scottish finance minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown, a Scot, was Chancellor of the Exchequer (the UK finance minister) from 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Brown was the Scottish politician serving as Britain's finance minister when this puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Animal came 'ither by boat, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken phrase, so the answer matches its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: coming hither by boat means having rowed here, said with a dropped h

explanation.surface: Someone with a dropped-aitch accent describes an animal that arrived by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ither signals a dropped h, so 'here' is said as 'ere' too.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small European species of deer, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: After a trip, three heads of delegation came to a Sussex town

indicators.note: after places what follows behind the first item, setting the order of the parts
three heads are the opening three letters of the word that follows

blocks.note: a run is a short trip, as in a run into town
the opening three letters of delegation

explanation.surface: A delegation travels to a southern English town after a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Arundel is a town in West Sussex, in southern England, known for its castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Arundel is a historic castle town in West Sussex, a county on England's south coast.

clue.text: Shed light on unhealthy upper-class reserve

blocks.note: ill means unhealthy
U is the old label for upper-class usage
a mine is a rich store or reserve, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: Someone explains the sickly reticence of the aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Illumine is a literary verb meaning to light up or to make clear, matching shed light on in both senses.

clue.text: Former spouse gets letter regarding expulsion from the Church

blocks.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
a letter is one kind of communication

explanation.surface: A divorced partner receives a letter about being thrown out of the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Excommunication is the formal ecclesiastical sanction cutting a person off from membership and sacraments.

clue.text: In Bali? Bishop claims to have been elsewhere!

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: runs across the end of the island's name and the start of the clergyman's title

explanation.surface: A bishop in Bali insists he was somewhere else at the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and exclamation mark break the run of letters visually but not in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea that the accused person was somewhere else when the crime happened, so the plural fits.

clue.text: A lass I knocked out in attack

indicators.note: knocked out suggests being knocked about out of shape, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: all six letters are used

explanation.surface: A girl is knocked unconscious during an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to set upon violently, a verb synonym of attack.

clue.text: Lithe, loose Miss Loe

indicators.note: letters set loose are free to move into a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a supple, free-moving young woman called Miss Loe.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome means slim, supple and graceful, a near synonym of lithe.

clue.text: Releases translation of Celan in America

indicators.note: a translation renders a text in new form, so the poet's name is rearranged
in places the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation for America

blocks.note: the surname of the poet Paul Celan
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: An American publisher brings out a translation of the poet Paul Celan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Releases' looks like a publishing verb but is the definition, in the sense of untying shoelaces.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlace a shoe or bodice is to undo its laces, which frees or releases it.

clue.text: Boffin, very stupid

blocks.note: a boffin is a clever scientist, informally a brain
dead means very in phrases like dead easy

explanation.surface: A scientist is described as extremely foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain-dead is informal slang for utterly unintelligent, so it serves as an adjective synonym for stupid.

clue.text: In a tantrum, ambassador is a venomous creature

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the outburst and the start of the diplomat

explanation.surface: A diplomat throwing a fit is likened to a poisonous animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a fast African snake whose bite carries a deadly poison.

clue.text: Half of a family dies horribly

indicators.note: something done horribly is mangled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Half of a family suffers a dreadful death.
explanation.definitionFit: We speak of relatives on the mother's or father's side, each being one of two branches of kin.

clue.text: Dicky, Gillian and Ruth almost fluent in three languages

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the name is dropped
dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: the name taken whole
the name without its final letter

explanation.surface: Two women, Gillian and Ruth, can very nearly speak three languages.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British slang for weak or unreliable, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilingual describes someone who speaks three languages well, matching fluency in three tongues exactly.

clue.text: Philosopher's follower is endlessly coarse, eccentric, with a twitch

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter goes
eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the word without its final letter
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A philosopher's disciple is portrayed as rough, odd and twitchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition takes Socratic as a noun: a Socratic is a follower of Socrates.
explanation.definitionFit: A Socratic is a disciple of Socrates or of his question-and-answer teaching method.

clue.text: Tabloid, understanding how Left is right

blocks.note: the Daily Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper
wise means having good understanding

explanation.surface: A popular newspaper shows political insight into how the left is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a left-leaning British tabloid, which feeds the political surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In a looking-glass image, left and right swap places, which is what reversing mirrorwise means.

clue.text: Swampy planet has some hydrogen

indicators.note: some means only part of the word, here its opening portion

blocks.note: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun
the opening two letters of the gas

explanation.surface: A marshy planet is said to contain some hydrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy and swampy both describe waterlogged, boggy ground, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Justify tirade supporting hostilities

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so it comes second

blocks.note: war is open hostilities
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: An angry speech is used to justify going to war.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant something is to provide grounds for it, a verb synonym of justify.

clue.text: Pig swallowing small fish and a bird

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the fish goes into the pig

blocks.note: a sow is a female pig
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: A pig gobbles up a little fish and a bird too.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Strong business partnership

blocks.note: first meaning: solid and unyielding
second meaning: a company, especially of partners

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise of a robust partnership; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for solid and steady and a noun for a commercial company, such as a law partnership.

clue.text: Mother, father, me and a French lady

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
da is an informal word for father
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family line-up: mum, dad, the speaker, and a woman from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title for a married woman, used as Mrs is in English.

clue.text: Queer old queen causing gossip in America

blocks.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
O is the abbreviation for old
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A strange former monarch sets tongues wagging in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In America' asks for the US spelling, without the u of the British form.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumor is unverified talk passed from person to person, which is what gossip is.

clue.text: Hinder keeper and defenders at the back

blocks.note: hinder as an adjective means at the back, as in hind legs
a guard keeps watch over something

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper and the back line obstruct the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hinder' reads as the verb to obstruct, but it is the adjective meaning rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard is the body of troops protecting the back of an army, so it is defenders behind.

clue.text: Depression finally seeming to be ominously close

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it accompanies

blocks.note: the final letter of seeming
to loom is to hang threateningly near

explanation.surface: A low mood appears at last to be threateningly near.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom is a state of low spirits or despondency, so it names depression in its emotional sense.

clue.text: Robert, perhaps, taking a light meal and a drink

blocks.note: herb Robert is a wild geranium, so Robert is one kind of herb
tea can be a light afternoon meal

explanation.surface: A man called Robert has a snack and something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert looks like a person's name, but herb Robert is a common wild plant; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb tea is an infusion of leaves or flowers in hot water, served as a beverage.

clue.text: Vacuous rich dislike the plating on some jewellery

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word loses its insides and keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of rich
odium is hatred or strong dislike

explanation.surface: Empty-headed wealthy people despise the cheap coating on their jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodium is a hard silvery metal often electroplated onto white gold and silver jewellery for shine.

clue.text: Lady sailor, Cathy, swam on, having been wrecked

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: all eleven letters are used

explanation.surface: A woman named Cathy keeps swimming after her boat is shipwrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtswoman is a woman who sails yachts, so she is a female sailor.
